title: Prime-axis data and Bell series
pvg_object: observable restricted to one valuation axis alpha e_p
forward_translation: Prime-power axis values become the Bell series; multiplicativity assembles local series into an Euler product where convergent.
reverse_translation: Taylor coefficients of the local series recover prime-power values within its formal or analytic domain.
lost_information: cross-prime dependence and global continuation are absent from a single local series
trigger: A multiplicative observable is defined by coordinatewise rules.
typical_output: exact local rational function or coefficient expansion
error_or_wall: Formal local algebra does not certify convergence or meromorphic continuation.
required_certificate: Separate formal identity, absolute-convergence region, and continuation theorem.
positive_example: For I_r, the Bell series is 1+y^(2r)/(1-y)^2.
counterexample: Matching the first few local coefficients does not prove equality of full Euler products.
anti_overclaim: Local factor discovery is a diagnostic until global analytic hypotheses are verified.
classification: Known exact local transform / convergence gate

title: First nonzero local exponent and candidate main scale
pvg_object: lowest valuation height at which a local observable is nonzero
ant_object: candidate rightmost singular factor and x^(1/k) scale
forward_translation: A local term c y^k suggests extracting a zeta or L factor at ks and hence a possible scale x^(1/k).
reverse_translation: A pole at s=1/k may indicate a k-th local layer but does not uniquely determine the geometry.
preserved_information: candidate leading exponent and character-power routing
lost_information: coefficient constants, cancellations, zeros, and residual analytic behavior
trigger: The Bell series begins at a known degree k.
typical_output: candidate singular layer and required factorization
error_or_wall: Local onset can be cancelled globally or masked by a vanishing residual factor.
required_certificate: Prove exact factor extraction, residual holomorphy, and nonvanishing or residue evaluation at the candidate pole.
positive_example: I_r begins at degree 2r, routing to a possible x^(1/(2r)) term.
counterexample: A formal y^k coefficient alone does not prove a pole at 1/k.
anti_overclaim: This is a candidate-layer heuristic until the analytic certificate is complete.
source_basis: Classical singularity analysis of Euler products

title: Pole order and logarithmic polynomial degree
pvg_object: multiplicity of a surviving local analytic layer after factor extraction
ant_object: pole order m and main term x^alpha times a polynomial of degree m-1 in log x
forward_translation: A pole of order m at alpha produces, under a valid transfer theorem, a log-polynomial of degree m-1.
reverse_translation: A log-polynomial main term suggests pole multiplicity but may also arise from combined singularities or differentiation.
preserved_information: singularity order and expected log degree
lost_information: exact coefficients and validity of contour or Tauberian transfer
trigger: An Euler factor is raised to a power or several factors share a pole.
typical_output: degree and coefficient formulas for logarithmic main terms
error_or_wall: Pole order does not control the remainder without vertical and boundary estimates.
required_certificate: Compute the Laurent coefficients and verify all transfer and growth hypotheses.
positive_example: The squared L((2r+1)s) factor yields x^(1/(2r+1))(B log x+C).
counterexample: A double formal factor can be cancelled by a zero of the residual product.
anti_overclaim: Expected log degree is not a certified asymptotic before cancellation checks.
classification: Known analytic routing law / cancellation gate

title: Residual local order and continuation half-plane
pvg_object: cancellation of low-degree coordinate-layer terms after removing model factors
ant_object: Euler product H(s) with local factors 1+O(p^{-m sigma})
forward_translation: If each residual local factor is 1+O(|y|^m), absolute convergence is expected for Re(s)>1/m.
reverse_translation: A residual convergence line constrains the first uncancelled local degree but does not uniquely recover it.
preserved_information: first uncancelled degree and an absolute-convergence threshold
lost_information: finite-prime behavior, zeros, continuation beyond absolute convergence, and vertical growth outside compacta
trigger: Model zeta or L factors have been extracted from a Bell series.
typical_output: holomorphic residual factor on a certified half-plane
error_or_wall: O-notation must be uniform on compacta; finite exceptional factors need explicit treatment.
required_certificate: Prove a summable prime majorant and distinguish holomorphy from nonvanishing.
positive_example: For I_r, cancellation through degrees 2r+1 leaves order 2r+2.
counterexample: Numerical cancellation at several primes does not establish a uniform Euler-product bound.
anti_overclaim: Absolute convergence of H does not imply a zero-free region for the complete Dirichlet series.
classification: Known convergence mechanism / analytic certificate interface
